brief:
Germany asked the International Court of Justice on Monday to dismiss a case filed by Nicaragua accusing Berlin of breaching the 1948 Genocide Convention by supplying arms to Israel, according to Al-Monitor. Nicaragua has argued that German weapons shipments facilitate Israeli military operations that violate the treaty's prohibitions.

The complaint marks an expansion of legal pressure targeting countries that supply military equipment to Israel. Germany's motion to throw out the case will force the court to examine whether it holds jurisdiction over the dispute and whether arms transfers can be held legally accountable under the genocide convention. The outcome could affect how international law treats military support to nations engaged in armed conflict.
dek: By Stephanie van den Berg THE HAGUE, Sept 7 (Reuters) - Germany asked the International Court of Justice on Monday to throw out acase brought by Nicaragua which accuses Berlin of violating the 1948 Genocide Convention because it supplies arms to Israel.…
title: Germany seeks dismissal of Nicaragua's genocide complaint at UN court
